name: Mary
bio:
The angel Gabriel appeared to Mary, a virgin of Nazareth engaged to Joseph, announcing that she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son, Jesus, who would reign forever on David's throne as the Son of God. When Mary protested that she was a virgin, Gabriel told her nothing was impossible with God, and pointed to her relative Elisabeth, thought barren, who was already six months pregnant with John the Baptist; Mary submitted, calling herself the Lord's handmaid. She hurried to visit Elisabeth, who, filled with the Holy Spirit, blessed her as the mother of her Lord; Mary responded with a song of praise, the Magnificat, exalting God for lifting up the humble and remembering his mercy to Abraham's descendants, and stayed with Elisabeth about three months (Luke 1:26-56).

Mary, engaged to Joseph, was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit before their marriage. An angel appeared to Joseph explaining this, and he took her as his wife, naming her son Jesus as instructed (Matthew 1:18-25). Her role throughout Jesus's life is detailed in the chapters ahead. Wise men from the east found the young Jesus with Mary and worshipped him, presenting gold, frankincense, and myrrh; soon after, Joseph fled with her and Jesus to Egypt to escape Herod's massacre of Bethlehem's children, returning only after Herod's death (Matthew 2:1-23). Along with Jesus's brothers, she once came seeking to speak with him while he was teaching; he used the moment to declare that whoever did God's will was his true family (Matthew 12:46-50).
